text:
maria: Quick heads-up — entering quiet window for Py/TS SDK publish at 22:00 UTC (in ~15m). Final checklist: signer verification, dist-tag plan, release notes push. @devex please ack and call out any blockers.

alan: ack. running signer check now. will post output.

release-bot: [deploy-schedule] Scheduled publish job queued: py-sdk v1.14.0, ts-sdk v2.3.0. ETA 22:03 UTC. CI green.

jen.k: I pushed the release-notes draft to /docs/releases/1.14.0.md — need one more review (changelog + breaking notes). cc @claire for wording on deprecations.

devops: Double-checking dist-tag plan: we do not flip 'latest' until the final canary smoke passes. plan: add 'canary' tags first, shadow for 30m, then promote. If we see signer mismatch at upload, we hold and revert tag.

alan: signer check output:
```
gpg: Good signature from "Redwood Release Key <releases@redwood.ai>"\nFilename: py_sdk-1.14.0.whl\nSHA256 OK
```
Looks good for py wheel. NPM sigs for ts coming in 2m.

sam: one contingency note — if any package fails checksum on PyPI or npm registry rejects the tarball, we should immediately: 1) pin package to previous dist-tag, 2) yank the problematic release (npm) / yank on PyPI (if necessary), 3) open rollback channel and notify customers. Example commands below:
```
# npm pin back to previous
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.2.9 latest
# npm deprecate as needed
npm deprecate @redwood/sdk@2.3.0 "temporary hold: bad signature"
# pip workaround: re-add previous wheel as 'latest' by re-tagging docs and callers
```
Also for emergency: we can set routing to dedicated nodes and throttle hosted until we clear. :rotating_light:

claire: release notes review: noted two deprecation lines — ok to call out the TS helper removal + migration path. I'll make copy edits and push in 5.

release-bot: [publish-job] py-sdk upload started (twine). Job: 3301012345-1.

maria: reminder — if we need to abort after upload, avoid pushing 'latest' tag and keep the canary tag. Only flip when both SDKs satisfy docs and smoke.

devops: npm sigs look good: gpg verify shows maintainer key. proceeding with canary tag for TS.

release-bot: [publish-job] ts-sdk published to canary tag v2.3.0-canary. Canary installation smoke test triggered.

alan: smoke logs (ts):
```
> node ./smoke-test.js --pkg @redwood/sdk@2.3.0-canary
ok 10 tests passed, latency median 45ms
```
No obvious regressions.

jen.k: I merged the release notes edits. final doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/releases/1.14.0.md — please thumbs up if ready. :thumbsup:

claire: :thumbsup: wording looks good. emphasize deprecation timeline to give users 2 weeks.

maria: decision time: promote TS to 'latest' and promote Py canary to 'latest' after 30m shadow if no regressions. Anyone object?

sam: no objections. just a note — if we observe increased error rates in the first 10m, auto-rollback policy triggers pin back and we notify via postmortem.

release-bot: [monitor] Canary metrics streaming: error rate 0.2% -> baseline 0.15%. keeping an eye.

maria: hold on promotion — seeing a signer mismatch on a subset of npm mirrors: some verify as good, others failing with 'public key not found'. Alan, can you sanity-check? :thinking_face:

alan: looking — it's a mirror propagation issue. The signature is valid but some mirrors haven't fetched updated keyrings. This should resolve within 10-15m. We can delay promotion.

devops: recommendation: pause promotion, extend canary window to 45m, and update release notes with a small FAQ entry about signature verification errors and patch steps. Also add a 'how to verify' snippet in notes.

jen.k: will add FAQ note now. small snippet: `npm install -g gpg` + `gpg --verify package.tgz.sig package.tgz`.

claire: can we add a quick outreach line for enterprise customers on Dedicated? they might see warnings. propose: "If you see signature errors, contact support and we'll confirm key propagation."

maria: agreed. Changing timeline: canary extended. No tag flips until 22:50 UTC. If signer mismatch persists beyond 22:50, we abort promotion and create rollback plan.

release-bot: [update] Extended canary window to 22:50 UTC per @maria.

sam: adding rollback checklist to this thread so it's discoverable:
- stop promotion, do not flip 'latest'
- pin npm & pip to previous versions (commands above)
- open incident ticket, include smoke logs and signer output
- notify customer success for inbound alerts
- create a short postmortem template

maria: all right — team ack if you saw the change and are good with extended canary.

alan: ack.

jen.k: ack, notes updated.

claire: ack, outreach drafted.

release-bot: [final] Canary period healthy at 22:46 UTC. Error rate back to baseline 0.14%. No further signer failures reported. Proceed?

maria: promote now. Let's flip TS then Py, wait 60s, then confirm telemetry.

release-bot: Promoted @redwood/sdk@2.3.0 to 'latest'. Promoted py-sdk 1.14.0 to 'latest'.

devops: post-promotion checklist: watch error rate and latency for next 10m. revert steps prepared.

sam: starting 10m watch. I'll call rollback if any sustained spike >3x baseline.

maria: thanks everyone — pushing release notes live and sending out release announcement in #general after 22:55 UTC. Great run.

release-bot: [announce] Release complete. Thread closed. :rocket:
